cards.question: What does it mean for an operation to be atomic?
cards.answer: Atomic operations are the smallest operations on data that either occur or do not; there is no half-done state.

cards.question: Why can two threads update an AtomicI32 without an inconsistent state?
cards.answer: They cannot both read the same value and update it at the same time, so the variable never ends up half-updated.

cards.question: Why is there no generic Atomic<T> in Rust?
cards.answer: Only specific types exist, such as AtomicBool and AtomicI32, up to the word size with AtomicUsize. Which atomics are available also depends on the architecture and OS.

cards.question: What does the Ordering parameter on atomic operations control?
cards.answer: It controls what guarantees we get about the relative ordering of operations. The CPU may still perform operations out of order, so two threads may observe assignments in different sequences.

cards.question: What is lazy initialization?
cards.answer: A pattern where a constant or expensive resource is calculated only when first requested and then stored for subsequent use.

cards.question: What race condition can a naive atomic lazy-init check-and-store have?
cards.answer: If two threads both see the unset value, they both restart the computation. Concurrent lazy initialization must be synchronized to prevent that.

cards.question: How do Once and OnceLock fix concurrent lazy initialization?
cards.answer: They are atomic helpers so only one thread runs the initializer. Later callers sleep until that first thread finishes call_once or get_or_init.
